NORMAL.description: No radiological abnormality detected in the chest cavity.
NORMAL.action: Routine follow-up as per clinical guidelines.

PNEUMONIA.description: Radiographic evidence of pulmonary consolidation or infiltrates consistent with pneumonia.
PNEUMONIA.action: Urgent clinical evaluation recommended. Consider sputum culture and appropriate antibiotic therapy.

glioma.description: Glial cell tumor originating from astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, or ependymal cells. Most common primary brain tumor.
glioma.action: URGENT: Immediate neurosurgical consultation. Requires histopathological grading (WHO Grade I-IV) and multidisciplinary oncology review.

meningioma.description: Tumor arising from meningeal tissues surrounding the brain. Typically slow-growing and often benign.
meningioma.action: Neurosurgical evaluation recommended. Serial MRI monitoring for growth. Surgical resection if symptomatic or growing.

notumor.description: No intracranial mass lesion identified on MRI examination.
notumor.action: Normal finding. Follow up as clinically indicated.

pituitary.description: Tumor of the pituitary gland (adenoma). May cause hormonal imbalances and visual field defects.
pituitary.action: Endocrinological workup recommended. Check prolactin, GH, ACTH, TSH levels. Ophthalmology referral for visual field testing.

skin_cancer.title: Dermatological Lesion Analysis
skin_cancer.subtitle: Skin Cancer Classification from Dermoscopic Images

akiec.description: Pre-malignant lesion caused by chronic UV exposure. Considered a precursor to squamous cell carcinoma.
akiec.action: Dermatological monitoring with possible cryotherapy, topical 5-FU, or photodynamic therapy. Sun protection essential.

bcc.description: Most common form of skin cancer. Locally invasive but rarely metastasizes. Appears as pearly, translucent papule.
bcc.action: Dermatological biopsy and excision recommended. Mohs micrographic surgery for high-risk areas. Regular follow-up.

bkl.description: Benign epidermal growth including seborrheic keratosis, solar lentigo, and lichen planus-like keratosis.
bkl.action: Generally no treatment required. Removal for cosmetic reasons or diagnostic confirmation if uncertain.

df.description: Common benign skin nodule of fibroblastic origin. Firm, dome-shaped, typically on lower extremities.
df.action: No treatment necessary unless symptomatic. Biopsy if diagnostic uncertainty.

mel.description: Malignant neoplasm of melanocytes. Most dangerous form of skin cancer with significant metastatic potential.
mel.action: URGENT: Immediate dermatological referral. Excisional biopsy with adequate margins. Staging workup including sentinel lymph node biopsy.

nv.description: Common benign mole (nevus). Proliferation of melanocytes forming well-circumscribed lesion.
nv.action: Monitor for changes (ABCDE criteria). Photographic documentation for comparison. No treatment unless atypical features.

vasc.description: Benign vascular proliferation including angiomas, angiokeratomas, pyogenic granulomas, and hemorrhage.
vasc.action: Usually benign. Treatment (laser, electrocautery) if cosmetically bothersome or recurrently bleeding.

No_DR.description: No diabetic retinopathy changes detected in the retinal fundus.
No_DR.action: Annual dilated eye examination. Continue glycemic control optimization.

Mild.description: Mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Microaneurysms only.
Mild.action: Ophthalmological review in 9-12 months. Optimize HbA1c, blood pressure, and lipid control.

Moderate.description: Moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. More than just microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR.
Moderate.action: Ophthalmological review in 6-9 months. Aggressive glycemic control. Consider referral to retinal specialist.

Severe.description: Severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy meeting the 4-2-1 rule criteria.
Severe.action: Urgent retinal specialist referral. Review every 2-4 months. Anti-VEGF therapy may be indicated.

Proliferate_DR.description: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy with neovascularization. High risk of vitreous hemorrhage and retinal detachment.
Proliferate_DR.action: URGENT: Immediate retinal specialist referral. Panretinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF injection indicated.

EOSINOPHIL.description: Granulocyte with bilobed nucleus and large eosinophilic granules. Elevated in allergic reactions, parasitic infections, and autoimmune conditions.
EOSINOPHIL.action: Correlate with complete blood count. Elevated eosinophils may indicate allergic disorder, parasitic infection, or eosinophilic syndrome.

LYMPHOCYTE.description: Agranular leukocyte central to adaptive immunity. Includes T cells, B cells, and NK cells.
LYMPHOCYTE.action: Correlate with differential count. Lymphocytosis may indicate viral infection. Lymphopenia may suggest immunodeficiency.

MONOCYTE.description: Largest normal leukocyte with kidney-shaped nucleus. Precursor to tissue macrophages. Role in innate immunity and phagocytosis.
MONOCYTE.action: Correlate with clinical context. Monocytosis may indicate chronic infection, autoimmune disease, or hematological malignancy.

NEUTROPHIL.description: Most abundant granulocyte with multi-lobed nucleus. First responder to bacterial infection and acute inflammation.
NEUTROPHIL.action: Correlate with total WBC count. Neutrophilia suggests bacterial infection. Neutropenia may indicate bone marrow suppression.
